**Mathematical statistics** — the theory of statistical inference read for itself — comparison and sufficiency of experiments (Blackwell, Le Cam deficiency), statistical decision theory, the sufficiency theorems (Fisher–Neyman, Basu, Bahadur) and bounds on estimation. Bayesian modelling is probabilistic-modeling (ADR-031).

| [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) v2 | For experiments on a finite parameter set, being at least as informative for every decision problem is the same as being able to simulate the other by a randomisation | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorem 8 with Theorems 1–3: for experiments with finitely many states and decision problems with bounded losses, α attains every loss vector β attains, in every problem, exactly when a Markov kernel turns α's observation into β's under every state. The direction from simulation to informativeness is Blackwell (1951); the finite converse is Sherman and Stein (1951); the general converse is proved in 1953. It is a qualitative order and says nothing about how much worse an incomparable experiment is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md) | The classical theorems on sufficient statistics need only the copy/discard structure of Markov kernels: Basu's theorem holds in every Markov category, and Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur need only strict positivity, not the existence of conditional distributions | Fritz (2020), [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md), read in [NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md), Theorems 14.5, 15.8 and 16.3 with the definitions of Sections 13–15. Sufficiency, completeness and ancillarity are stated with copy, discard, composition and almost-sure equality alone. Basu's theorem follows with no further axiom; Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur use strict positivity, which Stoch has although it lacks regular conditionals. The match with the classical theorems is shown in FinStoch (Fisher–Neyman) and through bounded completeness in Stoch (Basu), not for measure-theoretic Fisher–Neyman. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-161](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-161.md) v2 | In Zhao et al.'s (2025) and Chai et al.'s (2023) semantic rate–distortion frameworks, meaning is a latent variable with a known joint law with the observation, so their limits are indirect source-coding limits; Zhao et al.'s posterior-matching semantic distortion is, with KL divergence, exactly the information bottleneck, and with total variation a bound on the expected lost value of every bounded-loss decision | From the readings of Zhao et al. (2025), [LIT-793](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-793.md), Chai et al. (2023), [LIT-812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-812.md), and the survey of Xin, Fan and Letaief (2024), [LIT-823](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-823.md). | [THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md) v2 | A task-loss stitching penalty compares representations in one decision problem, through a fixed top network and a restricted map class, so it is not Blackwell's order: representations that are functions of each other can stitch differently, and a negative penalty shows the fitted map did not reproduce the layers it replaced | Bansal, Nakkiran & Barak (2021), [LIT-850](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-850.md), define the stitching penalty L_ℓ(r; A) − L(A), with L_ℓ(r; A) the least task loss of A's top layers fed r through a map from a simple family S, and use it to call one representation better than another. Read against Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), and [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), that ordering is one coordinate of the comparison of experiments with the decision rules cut down to A's head composed with S. It is not invariant under Blackwell equivalence, which the paper intends, and it meets Blackwell's order only where the fitted map reproduces the replaced layers exactly. The relations are this record's derivations from the paper's definitions, not the paper's. | Active |
| [THEORY-215](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-215.md) | A Hawkes process with a Lipschitz rate function and signed kernels has a unique stationary regime, which suitably started versions approach, when the Lipschitz-weighted absolute kernel mass is below one (a spectral radius below one, for a network) or when the rate is bounded | Brémaud and Massoulié (1996), [LIT-1035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1035.md), read in [NOTE-728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-728.md): Theorems 1, 2, 7 and 8, proved. Inhibition is allowed because the conditions use \|h\|. The conditions are sufficient, not necessary; the kernels are fixed in time; uniqueness is among solutions with finite mean intensity. In the linear excitatory case the condition is the branching ratio below one, but in the nonlinear signed case the spectral-radius quantity is a bound, not a branching ratio, and a bounded rate needs no bound on the kernels at all. Nothing is proved about cascade sizes or about what happens past the threshold. | Active |
| [THEORY-280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-280.md) v2 | The bisimulation metric between two finite Markov chains with observed states and a known cost bounded by 1 can be estimated without a transition model from independent samples of each chain's discounted state-pair occupancy, to accuracy ε with probability 1 − δ from a number of samples polynomial in the state-space sizes, 1/(1−γ), log(1/δ) and 1/ε² | Calo, Jonsson, Neu, Schwartz & Segovia-Aguas (2025), [LIT-948](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-948.md), read in [NOTE-763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-763.md). Bicausal occupancy couplings are characterised by constraints that use only each chain's sampled occupancy measure over consecutive state pairs. A stochastic primal-dual method on them gets an ε-accurate estimate with probability 1−δ from O((\|X\|\|Y\|(\|X\|+\|Y\|) + (\|X\|+\|Y\|)log(1/δ))/((1−γ)²ε²)) independent samples per chain. The states must be observed and enumerable, the cost known, and the samples drawn with restarts. A single running stream and latent states are outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-308.md) v2 | The neural Donsker–Varadhan estimator of mutual information is strongly consistent as an extremum estimator over compact families of critics, and, for critics bounded by M and L-Lipschitz in their d parameters, its uniform deviation from the population bound needs a number of samples set by d, M, L and the parameter radius, not by the data dimension | Belghazi et al. (2018), [LIT-256](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-256.md), §3.3 and App. 8.2.2–8.2.3, read in [NOTE-828](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-828.md). On a compact domain with Lebesgue densities, the supremum of the Donsker–Varadhan bound over some compact network family is within any η of the mutual information, and the empirical supremum converges to the population one almost surely. Uniform deviation ε needs Õ(d log d/ε²) samples for d parameters, under bounded, Lipschitz critics. The guarantee is for the exact empirical maximizer, not for gradient training. The finite-sample estimate is not a bound (Poole et al., [LIT-246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md)), and the proof has two gaps a reading found. | Active |
| [THEORY-318](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-318.md) v2 | A bound k on the max-information between a dataset and an analyst's chosen statistic multiplies by at most 2^k the probability that the statistic overfits that dataset, and an ε-differentially private mechanism on datasets of n points keeps k at most log₂e·εn, whatever the distribution on datasets | Dwork, Feldman, Hardt, Pitassi, Reingold & Roth (2015), [LIT-964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-964.md), Supplementary Material only, read in [NOTE-848](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-848.md) (Skimmed: the main text was not reached). Statistical queries on a discrete universe only, and a procedure that prevents inflation, not a correction for a search already run. | Active |
| [THEORY-391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md) v3 | Recovery of a k-sparse vector by ℓ₁ minimization from n random measurements in dimension N switches, as N grows with δ = n/N and ρ = k/n fixed, from near-certain success to near-certain failure across a curve ρ(δ) that, for Gaussian matrices, the authors' earlier face-counting theorems fix; in 2,948,000 optimizations at N = 200, 400 and 1600, eight non-Gaussian ensembles approached that curve in a way consistent with gaps shrinking as N^(−1/2), an exponent fitted on the same data, while at finite N the location depended on the ensemble | Donoho and Tanner (2009), [LIT-1160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1160.md), read in [NOTE-933](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-933.md) from arXiv 0906.2530v1. The Gaussian transition is a theorem of the authors' earlier papers, restated here. The universality is an observation from 2,948,000 optimizations at N = 200, 400 and 1600: strict finite-N universality is rejected, and agreement as N → ∞ is not rejected. Sparse and Hadamard matrices sit about one transition width low at small N. The title states only what was measured. Whether the agreement is a limit theorem is QUESTION-168. | Active |
| [THEORY-534](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-534.md) | The optimality of maximum likelihood was never one theorem: each historical proof holds under conditions its author left implicit, and of the classical counterexamples the practically important one is a parameter count growing with the sample, while Hodges-type superefficiency is confined to a set of measure zero | Stigler (2007), [LIT-044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-044.md), read in full in [NOTE-074](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-074.md). Fisher's 1922 proof rests on sufficiency, his 1925 proof on exact normality, and his private 1930 proof on multinomial data and smooth degree-0 estimators. Rigorous treatments (Wald 1943, Cramér 1946) came at the cost of unwieldy conditions. Neyman–Scott, where the MLE of σ² tends to σ²/2, is the failure Stigler weighs as practical; Hodges's superefficiency is possible only on a Lebesgue-null set (Le Cam 1953). It is a history: the theorem statements are reconstructions, and it says nothing about modern overparameterized models beyond one hedged warning. | Active |
| [THEORY-641](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-641.md) v2 | Under a well-specified, identifiable parametric Markov model of the target given the joint past, with ergodic lagged states, transfer entropy is the limit of the normalised log-likelihood ratio for the null of no dependence on the source's past, so it is Granger-sense predictive improvement; for finite-state chains the plug-in estimator is exactly that statistic, and under the null and the usual regularity it is asymptotically χ² with the difference in parameter counts as degrees of freedom | Barnett & Bossomaier (2012), [LIT-048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-048.md), read in full in [NOTE-053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md). The consistency result is a one-line consequence of Props. 1–2, and Prop. 2 is argued informally. The χ² null is imported from Wald (1943), whose regularity conditions are not checked. The non-central χ² for T > 0 is at best a local-alternative approximation. The finite-state identity and the Gaussian equivalence (half the Granger statistic) are exact. | Active |
| [THEORY-704](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-704.md) | In a stationary multivariate time series whose components include every relevant process, with interventions that are isolated exogenous changes and no instantaneous causation, a missing Granger-causal edge from a to b means intervening on a has no effect on b at the next step, non-ancestry means no effect at any horizon, and a set whose observed past blocks every back-door path into b's ancestors identifies the effect from observational data, as a multi-step linear-predictor coefficient in the Gaussian case | Eichler & Didelez (2007), [LIT-1164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1164.md), read in full in [NOTE-941](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-941.md). | [THEORY-709](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-709.md) | Mutual information between continuous variables can be estimated from k-nearest-neighbour statistics, with the joint k-th-neighbour distance in the maximum norm fixing the scale at which marginal neighbours are counted, so that the biases of the three entropy estimates largely cancel; the one approximation is a locally constant density, the systematic error scales with k/N, and exactness for independent variables is observed in every tested case but not proved | Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger (2004), [LIT-1163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1163.md), read in [NOTE-938](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-938.md) (formal sections in full, numerics at lower resolution). | [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md) | For experiments with finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, being at least as informative in every decision problem is the same as being reproducible from the other by a Markov matrix | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorems 4–6, read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md): the Sherman– Stein theorem, with a new minimax proof. With n states and finite outcome sets, write experiments as n × N Markov matrices P and Q. Every risk vector Q attains in every decision problem is attainable with P exactly when Q = PM for some Markov matrix M. The arbitrary-outcome extension is [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), still Proposed. A qualitative order: most pairs are incomparable, and it says nothing about how far apart they are. | Active |
| [THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md) | For finite X and Y, every information-bottleneck optimum at every β gives one encoder to all inputs sharing p(y\|x), so it is a stochastic coarsening of the minimal sufficient partition (the causal states of memoryless transduction); as β → ∞ the optima converge to that partition, but in general no finite β attains it, except when Y is a function of X | Shalizi and Crutchfield ([LIT-1240](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1240.md), read in [NOTE-976](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-976.md)) assert that the information bottleneck recovers the causal states as β → ∞. The record proves it, against stochastic encoders as well as partitions, and adds that every finite-β optimum factors through those states. So the IB hierarchy always nests under its top. It says nothing about whether optima at two finite β nest. Finite alphabets only. | Active |
